sections.content: Relative clauses add information about a person, thing or place without starting a separate sentence. *Que* is the most common relative pronoun, while *quien* and *donde* are useful for people and places in appropriate contexts.

items.spanish: La amiga que vive al lado siempre nos ayuda cuando tenemos problemas.
items.english: The friend who lives next door always helps us when we have problems.

items.spanish: Conozco a una familia que comparte muchas actividades con sus vecinos.
items.english: I know a family that shares many activities with its neighbours.

items.spanish: El vecino con quien hablamos ayer conoce bien a mi hermano.
items.english: The neighbour with whom we spoke yesterday knows my brother well.

items.spanish: La casa donde nos reuníamos de pequeños ya no existe.
items.english: The house where we used to meet as children no longer exists.

sections.content: You know possessives such as *mi* and *su* from A1. Inside a relative clause, *cuyo* does their job and means "whose": it joins the owner (*la amiga*) to the thing owned (*el hermano*). It agrees in gender and number with the thing owned, not with the owner, and no article follows it: *la amiga cuyo hermano vive en Madrid*, because *hermano* is masculine singular.

sections.title: Cuyo agrees with the thing owned
rows: cuyo + masculine singular: la amiga cuyo hermano vive en Madrid
the friend whose brother lives in Madrid
cuya + feminine singular: el vecino cuya hija estudia música
the neighbour whose daughter studies music
cuyos + masculine plural: la familia cuyos hijos viven cerca
the family whose children live nearby
cuyas + feminine plural: la vecina cuyas amigas viven cerca
the neighbour whose friends live nearby

items.spanish: Tengo una amiga cuyo hermano vive en Madrid.
items.english: I have a friend whose brother lives in Madrid.

items.spanish: El vecino cuya hija estudia música siempre nos saluda.
items.english: The neighbour whose daughter studies music always greets us.

items.spanish: Conozco a una familia cuyos hijos comparten muchas actividades con los vecinos.
items.english: I know a family whose children share many activities with the neighbours.

items.spanish: Mi vecina, cuyas amigas viven cerca, nos ayuda mucho.
items.english: My neighbour, whose friends live nearby, helps us a lot.

sections.content: The relative clause normally follows the noun it describes. Choose the relative form according to its role in the clause, not simply according to the noun before it.
